name: inprocess-obi-apb-gpio-pins-f1f5-fuzz
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex) and the pinned PULP apb_gpio target; no DMA model is part of this declaration, so the entry refuses F6 by name (unsupported-f6:no-dma-model)

the pin side is declared here: PADIN (offset 8) is the readable pad word, external_value 0 is the host driver value while no case carries a stimulus, and the pad resolves to the device's own out bit while its dir bit is high

trigger_writes repeat the reviewed PULP apb_gpio sequence GPIOEN(4), INTEN(24), INTTYPE_LOW(28, pin 0 = rise), PADOUT(12); the entry re-checks each against the profile's register map and the declared interrupt
PADDIR(0) must be set before the F5 case so pin 0 is device-driven: the rise that raises the device's own interrupt comes from the PADOUT write, not from the host
the target window is the profile's 4 KiB APB window at 0x40000000; the RAM image is the same fixed image the APB3 timer build uses
the cpu and target declare 50 MHz, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives both models

fuzz mode: the same declarations plus a declared F1 program length and a seed F4 that makes every pad an output before the F5 trigger sequence; the seed is an input precondition, not an execution permission
the F5 facts are also stated in configs/behaviors/pulp_gpio_f5_pins.json; the inline values must agree with it
